Perform normality test for multiple variables by groups

Source: R/ntest_by.R
ntest_by.Rd

This function performs a Shapiro-Wilk normality test on multiple variables in a dataframe by groups.

Usage

ntest_by(df, cols, group)

Arguments

df

A dataframe containing the data to be tested. It can be supplied directly (ntest_by(df = mtcars, ...)) or piped into the function (mtcars |> ntest_by(...)).

cols

<tidy-select> The numeric variables to test for normality, written as unquoted column names, e.g. mpg or c(mpg, disp). Selection helpers such as starts_with() or where(is.numeric) also work. Grouping variables are never tested.

group

<tidy-select> The variable that defines the groups, written as an unquoted column name, e.g. cyl.

Value

A tibble with one row per group and variable, containing the grouping variable(s) and the columns variable, statistic, p.value and method.

Details

Before running any tests, the function checks that df is a dataframe, that all variables in cols are numeric, and that each variable has between 3 and 5000 non-missing observations (the range shapiro.test() accepts) and is not constant within every group. If any check fails, the function stops with an error message explaining which groups or variables are affected. It then performs the Shapiro-Wilk test for each variable within each group and returns the results in a tidy format.

Groups are defined only by group. If df is already a grouped dataframe, that grouping is ignored and a short message says so (unless it matches group).

See also

ntest() to run normality tests for ungrouped data

Other normality tests: ntest()

Examples

# Perform a normality test for each group
ntest_by(df = mtcars, cols = mpg, group = cyl)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>     cyl variable statistic p.value method                     
#>   <dbl> <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                      
#> 1     6 mpg          0.899   0.325 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 2     4 mpg          0.912   0.261 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 3     8 mpg          0.932   0.323 Shapiro-Wilk normality test

# Test several variables by group, piping the data into the function
iris |> ntest_by(c(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width), Species)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   Species    variable     statistic p.value method                     
#>   <fct>      <chr>            <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                      
#> 1 setosa     Sepal.Length     0.978   0.460 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 2 setosa     Sepal.Width      0.972   0.272 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 3 versicolor Sepal.Length     0.978   0.465 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 4 versicolor Sepal.Width      0.974   0.338 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 5 virginica  Sepal.Length     0.971   0.258 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
#> 6 virginica  Sepal.Width      0.967   0.181 Shapiro-Wilk normality test
